chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Aban, from Abu Al-Abbas and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:
We heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pre-emption (al-shuf'ah) does not occur except for a partner who has not been distributed (his share).'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal in property co-ownership)

ai.seo_question: When does the right of pre-emption apply in Islamic partnership law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise temporal boundary for the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah), restricting it to partners prior to the formal division (qismah) of jointly owned property. In Shia jurisprudence, this ensures that a partner can acquire the share of another before it becomes distinct and alienable, thereby preserving the integrity of the co-ownership structure. The narration highlights the importance of timing in property transactions, a key principle in resolving disputes among co-owners.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban, from Abu Al Abbas, and Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who both said,
‘We both heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The pre-emption does not happen except for a partner who has not been distributed (his share)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban from abu al-‘Abbas and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “
We heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘ Al-Shuf ’ (one’s rights of pre-emption) is applicable only between two partners who have not concluded their partnership.’”
